answer: At each knoll of the network, a random subset of tasks is interleaved with dawn‑time spot checks whose answers are pre‑committed to an immutable ember hash; agents must submit matching responses or lose their stake. The protocol verifies the hash, rewards honest matches and slashes the bonded tokens of any identity that fails, forcing the attacker to lock up 10 % of total stake per fake identity. Consequently, creating a Sybil costs the attacker a non‑refundable deposit of 0.1 ETH and a 24‑hour waiting period before the identity becomes active.
